name: Rishikesh
tagline: Yoga capital of the world on the upper Ganges.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: Spring and autumn bring warm days, cool nights and the year's great yoga gathering; skip peak-summer heat, and note July-August's monsoon closes river rafting.

ourTake.lede: Rishikesh has two faces, the spiritual-yoga town and the adventure-rafting town, and the trick is knowing which you came for and staying on the right bank. For calm, take the quieter upstream side and a serious retreat rather than the backpacker strip near the bridges. Come in the cooler months when the Ganga runs clear and the heat is off; skip the monsoon, when rafting closes.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the Ganges, yoga and a serious wellness retreat within reach of Delhi.
ourTake.skipIf: You drink and want nightlife; the town is largely vegetarian and alcohol-free.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Ananda in the Himalayas
credentials: India's first destination spa (est. 2000)
Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice, repeat World's No.1 / Best Destination Spa (2005–07, 2012, 2019, 2020)
Named World's Best Wellness Retreat by Condé Nast Traveller (2023)
Set in the restored Viceregal Palace of the Maharaja of Tehri Garhwal
items.description: India's first destination spa and one of the world's greatest, a 100-acre Maharaja's estate above the Ganges, built for Ayurveda, yoga and genuine transformation.

items.name: Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa, Uttarakhand
items.area: Singthali Village (river road, ~30 km from town)
credentials: Taj Hotels luxury resort, 79 rooms, suites and villas (several with private pools)
Listed in the MICHELIN Guide (hotels)
Jiva Grande Spa and a 20,000 sq ft wellness sanctuary
items.description: A dramatic Himalayan-village resort on a private stretch of the Ganges, Taj polish, a 20,000 sq ft wellness sanctuary and a private river beach.

items.name: The Westin Resort & Spa, Himalayas
credentials: The Westin's first Himalayan resort (Marriott Bonvoy)
141 rooms including royal garden villas with private pools
Built around Westin's six pillars of well-being; Heavenly Spa
items.description: Marriott's Himalayan debut, a wellness-led resort of valley-view rooms, infinity pools and yoga-inspired programming near the world's yoga capital.

items.name: The Roseate Ganges, Rishikesh
credentials: Roseate Hotels & Resorts luxury boutique retreat, 16 villas
Featured by Sleeper Magazine for its design
Aheli spa; 17m infinity pool over the Garhwal foothills
items.description: A design-led boutique retreat of 16 standalone villas on the Ganges, quiet, intimate and beautifully made, with a 17-metre infinity pool over the valley.

items.name: Aloha on the Ganges by Leisure Hotels
items.area: Tapovan / Muni Ki Reti (by Laxman Jhula)
credentials: Leisure Hotels riverside resort, 74 rooms on the Ganga
Opposite Rajaji National Park; walkable to Laxman Jhula & Tapovan
Full-service spa and in-house yoga sessions
items.description: A riverside resort right on the Ganges near Laxman Jhula, well-placed for yoga, rafting and the old-town ghats, with a full-service spa.

items.name: EllBee Ganga View
credentials: Boutique art hotel on the Ganga at Triveni Ghat
Home to The Sitting Elephant rooftop restaurant
Steps from the Triveni Ghat Ganga Aarti
items.description: A boutique art hotel beside the Ganga at Triveni Ghat, rooms above the river, art on every wall and the evening aarti a short walk along the ghat.

items.name: The Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan
items.description: At dusk the largest ashram in Rishikesh gathers hundreds on the marble steps below its giant Shiva statue, and children of the ashram lead the fire prayer to the Ganga in unison, lamps, chanting and the river turning gold. It is the most soulful half-hour in town, and it is free. A private guide can secure a seat close to the priests and time your arrival before the crowd fills the ghat.

items.name: The Maha Aarti at Triveni Ghat
items.description: The grander, busier evening aarti, the town's main bathing ghat where the Ganga, Yamuna and mythic Saraswati are said to meet, ringed by lamplight and thousands of floating diyas. Rawer and more local than Parmarth, it is the fuller picture of a living pilgrim city. Come 30 minutes early; a guide keeps a multi-generation group together through the press.

items.name: Lakshman Jhula & Ram Jhula (the swaying footbridges)
items.description: The two iconic iron suspension bridges over the Ganga are the postcard of Rishikesh, pilgrims, cows, motorbikes and monkeys crossing above the green rush of the river. The century-old Lakshman Jhula has been closed and is being rebuilt, so the walkable pair today are Ram Jhula and the newer Janki Setu. Cross at first light before the heat and the crowds, then take chai on the far bank.

items.name: Janki Setu (the newest glass-floor footbridge)
items.description: The third and newest of the Ganga suspension bridges, with a glass-panel section and an evening light show that draws an easy crowd, a gentle, safe cross for grandparents and children while the older Lakshman Jhula stays shut. Temple bells and river chants carry from both banks. Best at blue hour when the lights come on.

items.name: The Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia)
credentials: Where the Beatles studied Transcendental Meditation, 1968, much of the White Album was written here
items.description: The abandoned meditation centre where the Beatles came to study with Maharishi Mahesh Yogi in 1968 and wrote much of the White Album, eighty-four egg-shaped stone meditation cells and a domed hall now swallowed by jungle and covered wall-to-ceiling in vivid graffiti and lyric murals. A rare, atmospheric hour that speaks to any generation. Open 10am–4pm; go early, carry cash for the ticket.

items.name: Parmarth Niketan (the ashram itself)
items.description: Beyond the aarti, the largest ashram in Rishikesh is a serene 1,000-room riverside campus of gardens, temples and a daily rhythm of yoga and satsang, the spiritual centre of the yoga capital. A private darshan and a quiet dawn walk before the day begins is a gentle introduction to ashram life without committing to a stay.

items.name: The International Yoga Festival
credentials: The world's foremost international yoga gathering, held here each March
items.description: For one week each March, Parmarth Niketan hosts the world's foremost yoga gathering, 70-plus hours of classes from master teachers worldwide, meditation, kirtan and discourse from India's leading spiritual voices, on the banks of the Ganga. The single best week to be in the yoga capital. Places and quiet accommodation should be arranged months ahead.

items.name: Swarg Ashram & the ashram belt
items.description: The traffic-free heart of spiritual Rishikesh, a riverside warren of ashrams, temples, book stalls and Gita Bhawan's scripture library, where you can walk barefoot along the Ganga with temple bells for a soundtrack. This is where the yoga-and-meditation world actually lives. An early-morning walk with a guide who knows which ashrams welcome visitors is the way in.

items.name: A private yoga & meditation session on the Ganga
credentials: Rishikesh is widely called the Yoga Capital of the World, an informal but universally used title
items.description: Rishikesh is where modern yoga went global, and a one-to-one dawn practice with a serious teacher on a riverside terrace, pranayama, asana, then silence as the mist lifts off the water, is the reason to come. Far more restorative than a group class. Your advisor can match teacher to level, from a first-timer to a lifelong practitioner.

items.name: Ananda in the Himalayas
credentials: Repeatedly ranked among the world's best destination spas
items.description: One of the world's great destination spas, a 100-acre estate around a Maharaja's palace high in the foothills, with Ganga views, Ayurvedic doctors, and week-long wellness programmes blending Ayurveda, yoga and Vedanta with international therapies. The ultra-luxury benchmark for the region and, for many, the whole reason to visit. Book a structured programme, not just nights, for the full effect.

items.name: The Vashishta Gufa (meditation cave)
items.description: A sixty-foot natural cave where the sage Vashishta is said to have meditated, ending in a Shiva lingam in total darkness, you sit on the mud floor in pitch black and silence, with a small ashram and a quiet Ganga beach just outside. The most profound meditation spot near Rishikesh, and utterly uncrowded. A short drive up the Badrinath road; go mid-morning.

items.name: White-water rafting on the Ganga
items.description: The Ganga above Rishikesh is one of the world's classic rafting rivers, cold, jade-green water threaded with named rapids from gentle Grade I to punchy Grade IV, run in stretches from Shivpuri (16 km) to the advanced Kaudiyala (36 km). Genuinely thrilling and safe with the right operator. Your advisor arranges a private craft, certified guides and a riverbank lunch, not the backpacker crush.

items.name: Bungee jumping & the Giant Swing at Jumpin Heights
credentials: India's highest fixed-platform bungee jump, 83 metres
items.description: India's highest fixed-platform bungee, an 83-metre leap from a cantilever built over a rocky Ganga tributary, plus a Giant Swing that free-falls before arcing across the gorge like a human pendulum. The adrenaline counterpoint to all the serenity, run to genuine safety standards. Perfect for a thrill-seeking teenager while the family watches from the deck.

items.name: The Flying Fox & cliff jumping
items.description: A one-kilometre zip-line that flings you across the river valley at speed, and cliff-jumping into deep Ganga pools at Shivpuri, the fun, lower-commitment end of Rishikesh adventure for a mixed-age group. Best paired with a morning raft. Book through one operator so the day flows and the safety cover is real.

items.name: The Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
items.description: A revered blue-spired Shiva temple high on a forested ridge between two river valleys, marking where Shiva is said to have drunk the ocean's poison and turned his throat blue. The drive up through Rajaji forest is half the pleasure; hardier pilgrims trek 12 km from Ram Jhula. Go early to beat both the heat and the queue.

items.name: The Kunjapuri Devi sunrise
credentials: One of the 52 Shakti Peethas of the goddess
items.description: A hilltop Shakti temple at 1,676 m with the finest sunrise in the region, a 360-degree sweep from the snow peaks of Gangotri, Bandarpunch and Chaukhamba on one side to the Ganga valley and the lights of Rishikesh on the other. One of the 52 shakti-peethas. Drive up in the dark for first light, then walk the ridge down.

items.name: The Tera Manzil (Trimbakeshwar) Temple
items.description: A striking thirteen-storey riverside temple, 'Tera Manzil' means thirteen floors, packed with shrines to countless deities, its terraces climbing above the Ganga to a top-floor view over the bridges and the town. A vivid, colourful hour and a favourite photo spot. Climb barefoot in the cool of the morning.

items.name: The Bharat Mandir
credentials: The oldest temple in Rishikesh, traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya
items.description: The oldest temple in Rishikesh, said to have been established by Adi Shankaracharya, tucked in the bazaar lanes of the old town with a black-stone Vishnu idol and a quiet, unhurried atmosphere far from the tourist bridges. A short, grounding stop that most visitors miss. Best combined with a wander through the old-town markets.

items.name: The cafes of Tapovan
items.description: The hillside above Lakshman Jhula is a warren of rooftop cafes serving good coffee, wood-fired pizza, Israeli and Tibetan food and fresh juice, most with a Ganga view and a slow, barefoot, post-yoga rhythm. The town's social heart between practice sessions. Late afternoon, with the river below and the hills going pink, is the moment.

items.name: Sattvic dining (the meat-and-alcohol-free town)
credentials: A legally alcohol- and meat-free holy town
items.description: Rishikesh and Haridwar are holy towns where meat, eggs, alcohol, and even garlic and onion in strict kitchens, are set aside for pure sattvic food: simple, fresh, vegetarian, cooked to nourish the practice. For a Jain or vegetarian traveller the whole destination is effortless. A private table at an ashram thali or a Tapovan cafe shows the range, from austere to genuinely delicious.

items.name: The Neer Garh Waterfall trek
items.description: A short, pretty forest walk off the Tapovan road climbs past tiered limestone falls to a couple of clear plunge pools where you can cool off, the most accessible of the local waterfalls and an easy morning for a family. Go September to November when the monsoon has filled it. Carry water shoes.

items.name: The Patna Waterfall trek
items.description: A steeper, wilder waterfall trek through forest and past a limestone cave to a 40-foot cascade, quieter and more of a hike than Neer Garh, and often combined with the drive up to Neelkanth. A satisfying half-day for able walkers. Best in the post-monsoon months when the water runs full.

items.name: The Garud Chatti Waterfall
items.description: A hidden, multi-tier fall a short walk from Lakshman Jhula, tucked in green forest and far quieter than the better-known falls, the reward is a private pool and birdsong rather than a crowd. The classic one-day loop links it with Neer Garh and Phool Chatti. A gentle, off-the-map morning.

items.name: Riverside luxury camping at Shivpuri
items.description: White-sand Ganga beaches upriver where premium camps pitch furnished tents by the water, bonfires, star fields, birdcall and a raft run at the door, without the roadside crowds of the town. A magical night for a multi-generation group who want the river without roughing it. Your advisor picks the camp with the beach and the standards to match.

items.name: Phool Chatti Ashram & waterfall
items.description: A tranquil riverbank ashram known for its structured silent-and-yoga retreats, with a small waterfall nearby and a stretch of Ganga far from the day-trippers. The place to go deeper than a single class. Even a day visit conveys the discipline and calm of ashram immersion.

items.name: The Har Ki Pauri Ganga Aarti (Haridwar)
credentials: Haridwar's holiest ghat and the principal Kumbh Mela bathing site
items.description: The grandest Ganga aarti in the country, at Haridwar's holiest ghat, where Vishnu is said to have left a footprint, thousands gather at dusk as giant flaming lamps are swung to roaring bells and the river carries a carpet of leaf-boat diyas downstream. Overwhelming and unforgettable. A guide arranges a safe raised vantage away from the densest crush, essential with elders or children.

items.name: The Mansa Devi Ropeway (Haridwar)
items.description: A cable-car ('udan khatola') swings up the hill to the wish-fulfilling Mansa Devi temple, with the whole spread of Haridwar and the Ganga laid out below, the fast, comfortable alternative to the 3-km climb and a highlight for children. Pair it with the Chandi Devi ropeway across the valley. Go mid-morning after the aarti crowds thin.

items.name: The Chandi Devi Ropeway (Haridwar)
credentials: One of Haridwar's Siddh Peethas
items.description: The second of Haridwar's hilltop goddess shrines, a Siddh Peeth reached by its own cable car over forested ridges, the pair of ropeways make a neat half-day of temple-hopping high above the town. Quieter than Mansa Devi and with wider Himalayan-foothill views. A guide books the combined tickets to skip the lines.

items.name: The Kumbh Mela ground at Haridwar
credentials: Site of the Kumbh Mela, among the largest human gatherings on Earth
items.description: Har Ki Pauri is one of the four sites of the Kumbh Mela, the largest human gathering on earth, when tens of millions come to bathe, and even on an ordinary day a guide can tell the story on the very steps where it unfolds. Context that turns a river ghat into history. The next Haridwar Kumbh falls in 2033.

items.name: Rajaji National Park (Chilla safari)
credentials: A Project Tiger reserve with one of India's largest wild elephant populations
items.description: An 820-sq-km tiger reserve of sal forest and elephant grass along the Ganga, home to Bengal tigers, one of India's largest wild elephant populations and 300-plus bird species, a private jeep safari from the Chilla gate is a genuine wilderness morning barely 20 km from Rishikesh. Elephant safaris have recently returned. The park runs mid-November to mid-June; a private jeep with a good naturalist is the way to go.

items.name: Devprayag, the birthplace of the Ganga
items.area: ~72 km up the Char Dham road
credentials: The sacred confluence where the Ganga is born, first of the Panch Prayag
items.description: The most sacred of the five prayags, where the turquoise Alaknanda and green Bhagirathi rivers crash together and are reborn as the Ganga proper, a dramatic confluence below a cliffside temple town, still largely untouristed. Stand on the sangam steps and watch two rivers become one. A rewarding day-drive up the Char Dham highway with a picnic on the way.

items.name: The gateway to the Char Dham Yatra
items.description: Rishikesh and Haridwar are the traditional starting point of the Char Dham, the Himalayan pilgrimage to Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath, and even without the full circuit, a curated first leg up the Alaknanda valley to Devprayag and beyond gives a taste of the sacred road. The classic Indian spiritual journey begins here. Your advisor can shape a comfortable multi-day itinerary or a single scenic day out.

items.name: A sunrise Ganga boat & morning dip
items.description: Before the town wakes, a small boat drifts you across still, mist-hung water while pilgrims take their dawn dip and temple bells start up on both banks, the Ganga at its most peaceful, a world away from the raft crowds. The quietest, most contemplative hour on the river. A private boatman and a warm shawl make it perfect for elders.

items.name: An Ayurvedic consultation & panchakarma
items.description: Beyond the yoga, Rishikesh is a serious Ayurveda destination, a proper doctor's consultation, a personalised regimen and a course of oil therapies or gentle panchakarma cleansing, from the world-class at Ananda to focused ashram clinics. Restorative in a way a spa day is not. Your advisor matches the depth of programme to how much time you have.

items.name: Kirtan & satsang evenings
items.description: As the aarti ends, the ashrams fill with kirtan, call-and-response devotional singing that builds for hours, and satsang, quiet talks with resident teachers. Sitting in on an evening of music and stillness is the most authentic, least touristed thing you can do in Rishikesh. A guide knows which sessions welcome visitors on any given night.

items.name: Gita Bhawan & the old-town bazaars
items.description: Gita Bhawan is a vast free pilgrim complex with a scripture library, riverfront steps and stalls of Ayurvedic remedies, rudraksha malas and Ganga-jal bottles, the shopping-and-scripture heart of pilgrim Rishikesh. A colourful, grounding wander for souvenirs with meaning. Best in the cool of the early evening.

items.name: The Ganga at Muni Ki Reti (river ghats)
items.description: The stretch of clean, swimmable Ganga between the bridges where locals and pilgrims take a holy dip on white-sand shallows, the water cold and glass-clear straight off the mountains. Even a barefoot paddle at the ghats is part of the pilgrimage. Mornings are calmest; a guide points you to the safe, gentle entries for a family.

items.name: A silent meditation retreat
items.description: For those who want more than a class, Rishikesh's ashrams run structured silent retreats, days of guided meditation, pranayama and stillness with no phone and no talking, the deepest form of what draws seekers here. Transformative even in a compressed few days. Your advisor arranges the right ashram, comfort level and teacher for a first retreat.

items.name: The Maa Chandi Devi & Neel Dhara Pakshi Vihar
items.description: Below the Chandi Devi hill, the Neel Dhara bird sanctuary on a Ganga barrage draws large flocks of migratory waterbirds in winter, an unexpected, tranquil counterpoint to Haridwar's intensity, and a treat for grandparents and birdwatchers. Come in the cool early morning with binoculars. Easily paired with the temple ropeways.

items.name: Evening at the Triveni Ghat feeding & floating diyas
items.description: Beyond the aarti itself, dusk at Triveni Ghat is a gentle ritual, feeding the sacred fish in the shallows and setting a leaf-boat lamp adrift on the current with a wish, a quiet moment even small children love. A soft, personal counterpart to the grand ceremonies. Buy a diya from the ghat stalls as the light fades.

items.name: Ananda in the Himalayas, cuisine
credentials: Dining within India's most awarded destination spa
Menus overseen by in-house Ayurvedic doctors and nutritionists
Repeat Condé Nast Traveller World's Best Destination Spa standing
items.description: Wellness cuisine at its most considered, Ayurvedic and calorie-conscious menus built around your programme, without ever feeling like a compromise.

items.name: Chidya Ghar, The Roseate Ganges
credentials: Signature restaurant of The Roseate Ganges (Sleeper-featured design)
Rare fine-dining focus on Kumaon/Garhwal hill cuisine
Roasted by Roseate patisserie on the same property
items.description: The city's most refined dinner, authentic Kumaon and Garhwal hill cuisine, millets and mountain produce, in a beautiful old-India room.

items.name: Riverside, Taj Rishikesh
credentials: Signature restaurant of Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa
MICHELIN Guide (hotels) property
Focus on the food of the Himalayan states
items.description: Himalayan home cooking done properly, Kashmiri, Himachali, Garhwali, Kumaoni and Nepali classics, with the Ganges below.

items.name: The Sitting Elephant, EllBee Ganga View
credentials: Rooftop restaurant of the EllBee Ganga View boutique hotel
Panoramic Ganga and Triveni Ghat views
A recognised old-town dining name
items.description: A rooftop table over the Ganga at Triveni Ghat, multi-cuisine vegetarian cooking with the best old-town river view in Rishikesh.

items.name: Little Buddha Café
credentials: A landmark Rishikesh café (est. 2007)
Consistently ranked among the city's best cafés (Tripadvisor / Tripoto)
Celebrated riverside rooftop views by Laxman Jhula
items.description: Rishikesh's most-loved café, a quirky treehouse of rooftop tables over the Ganga, a fixture of the town's traveller culture since 2007.

items.name: Bistro Nirvana
credentials: A recognised Rishikesh café (Tripoto / Himalayan Yoga Association)
Noted for well-executed international vegetarian dishes
items.description: The town's most polished café cooking, well-made Continental, Indian and Middle Eastern plates a notch above the traveller-café norm.

items.name: Chotiwala
credentials: A long-standing Rishikesh heritage eatery (decades-old)
A recognised old-town institution near Ram Jhula / Swarg Ashram
items.description: A Rishikesh institution of decades, thali-style pure-vegetarian cooking that still pulls pilgrims and locals to the old town.

items.name: The Ganga Aarti, the evening ritual
credentials: Rishikesh is a legally DRY, strictly vegetarian holy city, no public bars or alcohol sale
The dusk Ganga Aarti is the defining evening
Held nightly at Triveni Ghat and Parmarth Niketan
items.description: Rishikesh's real 'night out' is spiritual, not spirited, the sunset aarti on the ghats is where the whole city gathers after dark.

items.name: Riverside cafés & bonfire evenings
credentials: Alcohol-free rooftop cafés over the Ganga (Little Buddha, Bistro Nirvana and others)
Bonfire evenings at riverside camps toward Shivpuri
No alcohol served, chai, coffee and conversation
items.description: After the aarti, the town winds down over chai, cold coffee and a Ganga-side rooftop, or a bonfire at a riverside camp upstream.

plan.heading: 3 days in Rishikesh, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into a suite at Ananda in the Himalayas on the Maharaja of Tehri-Garhwal's palace estate, and take the medical consultation that sets your programme for the stay.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A quiet Abhyanga treatment at the Ananda spa, then time on the palace lawns above the Ganga valley as the light softens.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Ananda's restaurant with a river-valley view, ordering from the sattvic side of the menu.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: The old town and the ghats

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive down to Ram Jhula and walk the quieter Parmarth Niketan side, then a private hatha session on the ghat before the crowds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Cross to the Triveni Ghat area with a guide who knows the sadhu lineages, and see the Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia) walls and their murals in the afternoon calm.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Arrive early for the Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan, seated at the front, then a light supper back at the retreat.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: An early guided rafting stretch on the upper Ganga from Shivpuri, run gently rather than for thrills, with a riverside breakfast after.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A short forest walk toward the Neer Garh waterfall, then back for a closing spa treatment.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A private vegetarian thali dinner on the terrace, watching the last light on the far ridge.

items.name: Upstream / far bank (near Laxman Jhula and beyond)
items.description: Quieter, greener and retreat-oriented; best for wellness and calm.

items.name: Tapovan
items.description: The yoga-school and cafe cluster; suits longer-stay practitioners and the young crowd.

items.name: Riverside resort belt (towards Shivpuri)
items.description: Where the adventure camps and higher-end riverside stays sit; for rafting and river life.

events.name: International Yoga Festival
events.note: A week of teachers and practitioners from around the world at Parmarth Niketan, the town's signature gathering.

events.name: Ganga Dussehra
events.note: A river festival honouring the descent of the Ganga, with special aartis and bathing on the ghats.

events.name: Kartik Purnima / Ganga aarti season
events.note: The cool-season full moon brings especially devout riverside ceremonies.

events.name: Shivratri
events.note: A significant night for this Shiva-associated pilgrimage town, with all-night devotion.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Rishikesh is a sattvic town, so much of it is vegetarian and alcohol-free; dress modestly at the ghats and temples, and stay on the quieter Tapovan or Neelkanth side for calm above the day-tripper crowds.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Dehradun's Jolly Grant Airport (DED), roughly an hour's chauffeured drive to Rishikesh; from Delhi, a private helicopter charter to Dehradun shortens the journey considerably.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver for the temple town and the outlying ashram belt, and unhurried walking along the Ganga ghats and the two suspension bridges, which are closed to cars.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Airtel and Jio 4G/5G hold well in town; buy a local SIM at Delhi or Dehradun airport, as most eSIMs for foreign passports do not apply to Indian travellers here.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; cards work at hotels and better cafés but keep cash for riverside markets, temples and river guides; a small tip for drivers and boatmen is customary.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: October to April is kind, with clear days and cool nights; avoid May-June, when the plains heat climbs past 40C, and July-August, when the monsoon brings landslides and closes the rafting.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No airport in Rishikesh; fly to Dehradun (Jolly Grant, DED), a 45-minute drive away. Direct from Delhi (about 55 min, IndiGo/Air India) and Mumbai (via Delhi, about 3 hrs total). No lounge worth the wait at DED, so use the flagship lounge at your Delhi/Mumbai origin and keep the connection tight.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations beyond routine; carry standard Hepatitis A/Typhoid cover. Safe and calm town; the Ganga current is strong, so swim only where guided. Drink sealed or filtered water only.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Effortless: Rishikesh is a pilgrimage town and largely vegetarian, with no meat, alcohol, or eggs served in the temple belt. Jain food is widely understood. Chotiwala and the cafes above Laxman Jhula do reliable, clean vegetarian fare.
